description: Canonical single source of truth for Morning Puzzles rules, tutorials, move diagrams, and FAQs

games.title: SUDOKU
games.instruction: Fill every row, column, and 3x3 box with digits 1-9 without repeating.
games.objective: Complete the 9x9 grid with digits 1 through 9 so that no number is repeated within any horizontal row, vertical column, or outlined 3x3 box.
rules: Every row must contain digits 1-9 exactly once.
Every column must contain digits 1-9 exactly once.
Every 3x3 bold box must contain digits 1-9 exactly once.
Given clues are permanent and cannot be altered or moved.

valid_move.caption: Digit 5 placed in an empty square where 5 does not exist in its row, column, or 3x3 box.

invalid_move.caption: Digit 5 placed in a row or box that already contains another 5 (duplicate violation).

opening_anchors: Scan rows, columns, and 3x3 boxes that already have 6 or 7 numbers filled; only 2 or 3 candidates remain.
Use cross-hatching: trace a common digit (like 1 or 7) across perpendicular lines into an empty 3x3 box to eliminate squares.

faq.q: Do the numbers in a line need to be in numerical order?
faq.a: No. Digits can appear in any order as long as each number from 1 to 9 appears exactly once.

faq.q: Do arithmetic or mathematical sums matter in classic Sudoku?
faq.a: No. Sudoku is purely deductive placement. The numbers could just as easily be 9 letters or symbols.

games.title: SEARCH
games.instruction: Find all hidden words horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
games.objective: Locate every target theme word concealed within the letter grid in straight continuous lines.
rules: Words are spelled in straight lines: horizontal, vertical, or diagonal.
Words can run forwards or backwards in any direction.
Letters may overlap and be shared by multiple intersecting words.
Lines never bend, turn corners, or zig-zag.

valid_move.caption: Straight diagonal line tracing the word C-A-T forwards.

invalid_move.caption: Bent or zig-zag line tracing C-A-T around a corner (words must be straight).

opening_anchors: Search for rare letters in the word list (like Z, X, Q, or K) first, as they appear rarely in the grid.
Scan the word list for consecutive double letters (like EE, LL, or OO) and skim the grid for those pairs.

faq.q: Can words run backwards from right to left or bottom to top?
faq.a: Yes. Words can be oriented in any of the 8 standard compass directions.

faq.q: Can one letter belong to more than one word?
faq.a: Yes. Crossing words frequently share an intersecting common letter.

games.title: NONOGRAM
games.instruction: Shade cells to match row and column run counts with at least one blank between runs.
games.objective: Deduce which cells to shade black so that consecutive shaded runs match every outer row and column clue.
rules: Numbers outside the grid indicate the lengths of consecutive shaded blocks in that line.
Multiple numbers mean multiple shaded blocks in that exact sequential order.
Every pair of distinct shaded blocks must be separated by at least one empty white cell.
Lines with a 0 or empty clue contain zero shaded cells.

valid_move.caption: Clue '1 1' with one shaded cell, a white blank space, and a second shaded cell.

invalid_move.caption: Clue '1 1' drawn as two touching shaded cells, forming an illegal block of 2.

opening_anchors: Look for full-line clues: if a line clue equals the grid width, shade the entire line immediately.
Use clue overlap: when a clue number is greater than half the grid width, the middle cells must always be shaded regardless of alignment.

faq.q: Must there be an empty space between two shaded blocks?
faq.a: Yes. Separate numbers in a clue always require at least one blank cell between their blocks.

faq.q: Do the clues specify the order of the blocks?
faq.a: Yes. Row clues read left-to-right; column clues read top-to-bottom.

games.title: STARS
games.instruction: Place 2 stars in every row, column, and outlined region without touching, even diagonally.
games.objective: Position stars on the board so that every row, column, and outlined region has the required star count with no adjacent stars.
rules: Every row and column must contain exactly the target star quota (1 or 2 stars).
Every outlined geometric region must contain exactly the target star quota.
No two stars may touch each other anywhere—not orthogonally, and not diagonally.
Every placed star creates an 8-cell empty buffer zone surrounding it.

valid_move.caption: Stars placed with a gap of at least one empty square between them in all directions.

invalid_move.caption: Two stars touching at their diagonal corners (stars can never touch diagonally).

opening_anchors: Find anchor regions with only 1 or 2 total cells. A 1-cell region requiring 1 star must immediately hold a star!
Whenever a star is placed, immediately dot all 8 surrounding cells—none of them can ever hold a star.

faq.q: Can two stars be in the same row if they belong to different regions?
faq.a: No. The row quota is strict; every row across the entire board has the exact same limit.

faq.q: Does 'not touching diagonally' apply across the whole board?
faq.a: No. It applies only to immediate neighboring squares that share a corner point.

games.title: JUMBLE
games.instruction: Unscramble each clue word, then use the circled letters to solve the final pun.
games.objective: Unscramble each anagram word into its letter boxes, collect the circled letters, and arrange them to answer the pun riddle.
rules: Each jumbled word unscrambles into a single valid English word matching the box count.
Circled letter boxes highlight specific letters needed for the bonus pun.
The collected circled letters form an anagram pool for the punchline answer.
Letter blanks and punctuation in the final punchline guide word boundaries.

valid_move.caption: Unscrambled clue word 'BRAIN' with circled letters correctly placed into clue boxes.

invalid_move.caption: Misspelled or incorrect anagram that leaves circled letters unusable for the riddle.

opening_anchors: Unscramble the shortest clue words first to quickly secure your first circled mystery letters.
Read the punchline riddle carefully; humor and puns usually reveal the theme of the bonus answer.

faq.q: Are the circled letters in order when copied to the final answer?
faq.a: No. The circled letters form an anagram pool and must be unscrambled to solve the pun.

faq.q: What if an anagram word has multiple valid English solutions?
faq.a: Only one solution will yield the exact letters needed to solve the final riddle pun.

games.title: BINARY
games.instruction: Fill every cell with 0 or 1 so no more than two identical numbers are adjacent.
games.objective: Fill the entire grid with 0s and 1s adhering to adjacency, equal balance, and line uniqueness rules.
rules: No more than two identical numbers may be placed side-by-side (no '000' or '111').
Every row and column must contain an equal number of 0s and 1s.
No two rows may be identical, and no two columns may be identical.
All given numbers are fixed and permanent.

valid_move.caption: Alternating sequence '1 0 1 0' with no three identical digits in a row.

invalid_move.caption: Three identical numbers in a row '1 1 1' (maximum allowed adjacent is two).

opening_anchors: Look for pairs: whenever you see two identical digits ('00' or '11'), the cells on both ends must be the opposite digit.
Look for sandwiches: whenever two identical digits are separated by one blank ('0_0' or '1_1'), the middle cell must be the opposite.

faq.q: Can diagonal lines have three identical digits?
faq.a: Yes. The 'no three in a row' rule applies strictly to horizontal rows and vertical columns.

faq.q: What does equal balance mean?
faq.a: On an 8x8 board, every single row and column must contain exactly four 0s and four 1s.

games.title: MINES
games.instruction: Deduce all hidden mines using numbers showing how many adjacent cells contain mines.
games.objective: Deduce the exact locations of all hidden mines without guessing, using numeric neighbor hints.
rules: A number in a cell indicates how many of its 8 surrounding neighbors contain a mine.
Empty unnumbered cells are safe playable territory.
Mark confirmed mines with a flag or star.
Every puzzle is logically solvable from given clues with zero guesswork.

valid_move.caption: Cell with clue '1' having exactly one flagged mine neighbor.

invalid_move.caption: Cell with clue '1' having two flagged mine neighbors (overloaded clue).

opening_anchors: Zero clues ('0') are instant safe zones: all 8 surrounding neighbor cells are completely mine-free.
Corner clues: a '1' in a corner cell with only one hidden neighbor must have the mine in that single neighbor.

faq.q: Do diagonal cells count toward a number clue?
faq.a: Yes. Clue numbers count all 8 neighboring cells (orthogonal and diagonal).

faq.q: Can a numbered cell contain a mine?
faq.a: No. Numbered cells are always safe revealed territory; mines are hidden in blank cells.

games.title: TENTS
games.instruction: Pitch tents next to trees without any tents touching, matching row and column quotas.
games.objective: Pitch a tent for every tree on the board such that tents pair 1:1 orthogonally and never touch each other.
rules: Every tree must have exactly one tent pitched orthogonally adjacent to it (up, down, left, right).
Tents can never touch another tent—neither orthogonally nor diagonally.
Numbers outside the grid specify the exact count of tents in that row or column.
Tents may be adjacent to trees other than their own assigned partner.

valid_move.caption: Tent pitched orthogonally adjacent to a tree with an empty buffer around the tent.

invalid_move.caption: Two tents touching diagonally (tents can never touch even at corners).

opening_anchors: Check rows and columns with a clue of '0': immediately eliminate and cross out all cells in that line.
Trees with only one available empty orthogonal neighbor must pitch their tent into that single spot.

faq.q: Can a tent be attached diagonally to its tree?
faq.a: No. A tent must connect to its tree orthogonally (sharing a flat side, not a corner).

faq.q: Can a tent touch a tree that belongs to another tent?
faq.a: Yes. Tents can touch other trees, but tents can NEVER touch another tent.

games.title: BRIDGES
games.instruction: Connect islands with up to two orthogonal bridges matching numbers into one network.
games.objective: Connect all numbered islands together into a single continuous interconnected network using horizontal and vertical bridges.
rules: Bridges run horizontally or vertically between islands, never crossing each other or islands.
At most two bridges can connect any single pair of islands.
The number on an island equals the total count of bridges connected to it.
All islands must form one single connected network when complete.

valid_move.caption: Two parallel orthogonal bridges connecting island 3 to island 2.

invalid_move.caption: Three bridges connecting two islands (maximum allowed between two islands is two).

opening_anchors: Look for high-value corner islands: a corner island marked '4' with only 2 directions available must send 2 bridges each way.
An island marked '1' that only has one possible neighbor must immediately connect its single bridge.

faq.q: Can bridges be drawn diagonally?
faq.a: No. Bridges must run strictly horizontal or vertical.

faq.q: Can the completed puzzle have isolated subnetworks?
faq.a: No. All islands must link together into a single unified continuous group.

games.title: KILLER
games.instruction: Fill the grid with digits 1-9 so cages sum to their clue without repeating digits.
games.objective: Solve the Sudoku grid while satisfying all dotted cage boundary sums with non-repeating digits.
rules: Standard Sudoku rules apply: digits 1-9 once per row, column, and 3x3 block.
Dashed outline cages display a target sum in their upper-left corner.
Digits inside a cage must add up exactly to the cage's clue sum.
Digits can never repeat within the same cage.

valid_move.caption: Cage of size 2 with sum '3' filled with digits 1 and 2 (1 + 2 = 3).

invalid_move.caption: Cage with sum '4' filled with repeating digits 2 and 2 (digits cannot repeat in a cage).

opening_anchors: Look for unique sum combinations: a 2-cell sum of 3 must be [1, 2]; a 2-cell sum of 4 must be [1, 3]; a 2-cell sum of 17 must be [8, 9].
Use the Rule of 45: every row, column, and 3x3 block always sums up to exactly 45.

faq.q: Can a digit repeat in a cage if it spans across different 3x3 boxes?
faq.a: No. Digits can NEVER repeat within any cage, regardless of boundaries.

faq.q: Are starting clues printed as regular Sudoku numbers?
faq.a: Usually Killer Sudoku boards begin completely empty, relying entirely on cage sums.

games.title: CRYPTOGRAM
games.instruction: Deduce the hidden quotation where each letter is consistently substituted with another.
games.objective: Decode the secret cipher quotation by discovering which letter replaces each ciphertext letter throughout the puzzle.
rules: Each ciphertext letter represents one unique substitute plaintext letter throughout the entire puzzle.
Punctuation, apostrophes, and word spacing remain unchanged and preserved.
No letter substitutes for itself.
Once a substitution is determined, it applies to every occurrence of that letter.

valid_move.caption: Consistent substitution: every ciphertext 'K' is decoded as plaintext 'E'.

invalid_move.caption: Inconsistent substitution: decoding ciphertext 'K' as 'E' in one word and 'O' in another.

opening_anchors: Identify single-letter words: in English, single-letter words are almost always 'A' or 'I'.
Look for common short words like 'THE', 'AND', 'THAT', and letters following apostrophes ('T, 'S, 'LL).

faq.q: Can a ciphertext letter stand for itself?
faq.a: No. In standard cryptograms, a letter never encodes to itself.

faq.q: What is the most common letter in English text?
faq.a: The letter 'E' is by far the most frequent, followed by 'T', 'A', 'O', and 'I'.

games.title: TANGO
games.instruction: Fill grid with suns and moons so equal symbols match and opposite symbols differ.
games.objective: Place suns (☀️) and moons (🌙) so that no three identical symbols touch, lines balance, and relational cues are satisfied.
rules: No more than two identical symbols may be adjacent horizontally or vertically.
Each row and column must contain an equal number of suns and moons.
Cells separated by '=' must contain the exact same symbol.
Cells separated by 'x' must contain opposite symbols.

valid_move.caption: Cells with '=' clue filled with identical symbols (two suns).

invalid_move.caption: Three identical symbols in a row '☀️ ☀️ ☀️' (maximum allowed adjacent is two).

opening_anchors: Satisfy 'x' (opposite) clues: if one cell is given, the adjacent cell is immediately known.
Watch for symbol pairs: two adjacent suns ('☀️☀️') must be flanked on both sides by moons ('🌙').

faq.q: What does the 'x' mark between cells mean?
faq.a: It means the two cells must have opposite symbols (one sun and one moon).

faq.q: Does the two-in-a-row limit apply diagonally?
faq.a: No. The adjacency restriction applies strictly to horizontal and vertical lines.

games.title: LADDER
games.instruction: Deduce words changing one letter at a time to transform start word into end word.
games.objective: Navigate from the top start word to the bottom target word in sequential steps, changing exactly one letter at each rung.
rules: Each rung of the ladder must form a valid, recognized English word.
You may change exactly one letter from the previous word at each step.
Letter positions cannot be anagrammed, rearranged, or swapped.
The ladder is complete when you reach the target word in the allotted rungs.

valid_move.caption: Single letter change from C-A-R-T to D-A-R-T (valid English word).

invalid_move.caption: Changing two letters at once from C-A-R-T to D-A-R-K (only one letter change allowed).

opening_anchors: Compare the start and target words to count how many letters they already share in identical positions.
Work bidirectionally: if stuck moving downward from the start, try working upward from the target word.

faq.q: Can I rearrange the letters while changing one?
faq.a: No. All unchanged letters must remain in their exact same positions.

faq.q: Are proper nouns like names allowed as intermediate words?
faq.a: No. Every step must be a standard dictionary English word.

games.title: WHEEL
games.instruction: Find words of 4+ letters using the wheel letters, always including the center letter.
games.objective: Form as many valid English words of 4 or more letters as possible from the circular letter wheel.
rules: Every word must be at least 4 letters long.
Every word must contain the designated central hub letter.
Letters can only be used as many times as they appear in the wheel.
At least one 9-letter pangram exists that uses every single letter in the wheel.

valid_move.caption: Word 'GLOW' uses letters from the wheel and contains the required center letter 'O'.

invalid_move.caption: Word 'WING' spelled without using the required central hub letter 'O'.

opening_anchors: Look for common prefixes (like RE-, UN-, DE-) and suffixes (like -ING, -ED, -TION) among the rim letters.
Keep hunting for the 9-letter master word that utilizes every letter on the wheel.

faq.q: Can I use letters more than once in a single word?
faq.a: Only if that letter appears multiple times on the wheel rim.

faq.q: Do words without the center letter count?
faq.a: No. Any word that omits the central hub letter is strictly invalid.

games.title: LIGHTS
games.instruction: Place bulbs to illuminate corridors so numbered blocks match and no bulbs shine on each other.
games.objective: Place lightbulbs in corridors so every white cell is illuminated without any two bulbs facing each other.
rules: Bulbs emit beams of light horizontally and vertically along corridors until blocked by black barrier blocks.
Every white grid square must be illuminated by at least one lightbulb.
No two lightbulbs can illuminate or shine upon each other (no shared line of sight).
Numbers on black blocks specify how many bulbs must touch that block orthogonally.

valid_move.caption: Two lightbulbs placed on opposite sides of a barrier block (line of sight is blocked).

invalid_move.caption: Two lightbulbs in direct open line of sight of each other along a corridor.

opening_anchors: Locate '0' barrier blocks: place small dots or crosses on all 4 adjacent cells; no bulbs can go there.
Locate '4' barrier blocks (or corner '2's): all available orthogonal spaces around them must immediately hold bulbs.

faq.q: Can light beams shine diagonally?
faq.a: No. Light travels strictly in orthogonal horizontal and vertical straight lines.

faq.q: Can light pass through black barrier blocks?
faq.a: No. Black blocks completely obstruct and stop light beams.

games.title: LOOP
games.instruction: Draw a single continuous closed loop around numbers indicating surrounding line count.
games.objective: Connect dots with horizontal and vertical line segments to form one continuous closed loop that never branches or crosses.
rules: A number inside a cell specifies exactly how many of its 4 boundary edges belong to the loop.
Cells with no number may have any count of boundary edges (0, 1, 2, or 3).
The loop must form a single continuous closed circuit.
The loop can never branch, fork, intersect, or cross itself.

valid_move.caption: Cell with clue '3' having exactly three connected boundary edges drawn around it.

invalid_move.caption: Fork or branch in the line (loop must be a single path without intersections).

opening_anchors: Clue '0' is an absolute barrier: cross out all four edges around every 0 cell immediately.
Adjacent '3' clues: two neighboring 3s always share an outer line pattern and have their common divider filled.

faq.q: Can there be multiple small loops on the board?
faq.a: No. There must be exactly one single closed loop incorporating all satisfied clues.

faq.q: Can the loop line connect dots diagonally?
faq.a: No. Lines run strictly horizontally or vertically between adjacent grid dots.

games.title: TOWERS
games.instruction: Place building heights 1-5 so edge clues match how many towers are visible in that line.
games.objective: Fill each row and column with skyscrapers of heights 1 to N such that outside clues match visible towers from that vantage point.
rules: Every row and column must contain building heights 1 through N with no duplicates.
Numbers outside the grid indicate how many buildings can be seen looking into that line.
Taller buildings conceal and hide any shorter buildings situated behind them.
All given starting numbers and edge clues are fixed.

valid_move.caption: Line with clue '1' seeing tallest building (5) first, hiding all others behind it.

invalid_move.caption: Line with clue '1' placed with shorter building (2) in front (at least two towers would be seen).

opening_anchors: Clues of '1': the very first building in that line must be the maximum height (e.g., 5).
Clues of '5' (on a 5x5): the buildings in that line must ascend in strict sequential order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

faq.q: Does a taller building hide buildings that are further down the line?
faq.a: Yes. Any building shorter than a preceding building in the line of sight is hidden.

faq.q: Can heights repeat in a row or column?
faq.a: No. Each row and column forms a Latin square where each height appears exactly once.

games.title: INEQUALITY
games.instruction: Fill grid with digits 1-5 so each digit appears once per line and inequality signs hold.
games.objective: Fill the grid with numbers 1 to N so no digit repeats in any row or column and all '<' and '>' signs are honored.
rules: Each row and column must contain digits 1 through N exactly once.
Inequality signs ('<' and '>') between adjacent cells must be strictly honored.
The open end of the sign always points to the larger number.
Initial starting digits and inequality signs cannot be changed.

valid_move.caption: Digits satisfying inequality: 2 < 4 correctly placed in adjacent cells.

invalid_move.caption: Violation of inequality: placing 5 < 3 (5 is greater than 3).

opening_anchors: Look for chains of inequality signs: a chain of A < B < C < D on a 5x5 grid heavily restricts the possible values.
The cell at the largest end of multiple inequality signs can never be 1; the smallest end can never be N.

faq.q: Do inequality signs apply to non-adjacent cells?
faq.a: No. They apply strictly to the two adjacent squares directly bordering the sign.

faq.q: Can digits repeat in the same row if they satisfy the inequality?
faq.a: No. Every digit must be unique within its row and within its column.
